content:
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] 2026-03-15 02:47 UTC - KV cache eviction surge detected in prod-us-west-2. Paging threshold breached, streaming clients experiencing token cadence stalls and partial flushes. Severity: P1. Thread opened for triage.

alex: seeing the alert + graphs. unique_keys jumped from ~1.2M to ~4.8M in ~10m. eviction_rate spiked and paging to disk started. looks like continuous-batching is producing many small unique prefixes.

priya: pinging oncall. @sam_oncall can you take?

sam_oncall: taking this. quick summary? current impact?

alex: quick: PR#3456 (batch-splitter tweak) merged ~02:05 UTC. We started seeing a key-combinatoric pattern in the cache where session prefixes aren't normalized, so same logical contexts are creating many entries. Streaming clients see partial flush gaps ~200-800ms.

ben: copying relevant log snippets:
```
2026-03-15T02:40:12Z serve-12 kv_cache.cpp:142 WARN key=ctx:conv:12345:prefix=[a,b,c...] size=1
2026-03-15T02:41:02Z serve-12 kv_cache.cpp:142 INFO unique_keys=1200000
2026-03-15T02:46:50Z serve-12 kv_cache.cpp:142 INFO unique_keys=4750000
2026-03-15T02:47:05Z stream-21 stream.cpp:88 WARN partial_flush session=conv:12345 gap_ms=450
```

marta: customer impact so far: multiple streaming customers reported increased end-to-end latency and a couple observed stuck streams that resumed after ~1s. CS reported tickets from acct-345 and acct-912. No perceived data loss.

li: paging metrics: agg_disk_iops spike + io_wait up on serve-08/09/12. swap usage climbed on serve-09. Disk backlog queue length ~2k ops. Paging is likely amplifying tail latency.

sam_oncall: mitigation plan (short-term):
1) disable batch_splitter feature flag to stop key explosion
2) throttle streaming concurrency for affected frontends (reduce to 60%)
3) apply temporary per-session prefix cap eviction (runtime flag)
4) roll back PR#3456 if flag flip insufficient
Do we have a quick toggle?

devops-bot: Runtime config store writable. Feature flag path: feature.batch_splitter.enabled.

alex: prepared a defensive hotfix to enforce prefix_count limit:
```
if (session.prefix_count > 256) {
  compact_prefixes(session);
  metrics.increment("kv.prefix_truncate");
}
```
But safer to flip the flag first and then rollback.

ben: I can flip the flag now via runtime config. Doing: set feature.batch_splitter.enabled=false (02:55:10 UTC).

ben: (reaction :thumbsup:) flag toggle applied.

marta: watching dashboards -> eviction rate down ~45% in 3m. unique_keys trending down from 4.7M -> 2.3M. streaming error rate dropping.

li: disk backlog clearing but slowly. I'll start a controlled drain of serve-09 (lowest utilization) to free memory and stop continuous paging there.

jose: starting customer comms draft: "We observed elevated streaming latency and partial stalls starting ~02:40 UTC due to an internal batching change; we’re rolling back and mitigating. No data loss, working on fix. Will update in 30m." Sending to CS for review.

sam_oncall: devops-bot, can we canary a rollback of PR#3456? I'd prefer flip+rollback: flip -> observe 10min -> canary rollback -> full rollback if canary looks good.

devops-bot: Canary rollback job created. Will route 5% traffic to rollback group in us-west-2.

alex: canary logs look clean. unique_keys on canary nodes stable ~1.1M, no partial flushes seen in the past 5m.

marta: performance: canary streaming p50/p95 back to baseline. No paging spikes on canary. Recommend proceed.

sam_oncall: proceed with full rollback.

devops-bot: Rollback started at 03:12 UTC -> full rollback completed at 03:18 UTC across us-west-2.

ben: confirming rollback completed. feature flag is still false. full roll back of PR#3456 tag v1.23.1 -> v1.23.0 done.

marta: post-rollback metrics: unique_keys dropped to ~1.15M, eviction rate baseline, streaming error rate ~1.1% (normal ~0.8%). Partial flush incidents reduced to baseline frequency. Disk backlog cleared over ~20m.

sam_oncall: handing over to eng-ml / platform for root cause RCA and long-term fix. @priya please open the incident ticket and coordinate patch.

priya: creating INC-2026-0315-kv-batch-regression with logs, diffs, and mitigation timeline. assigning owner: alex (fix) and li (infra follow-up). ETA for permanent fix: 24-48h.

alex: proposed long-term fixes: 1) per-session prefix normalization before caching; 2) aggressive background compaction job; 3) unit tests for batch-splitter combinatorics; 4) limit default prefix_count to 128.

li: infra followups: 1) add alert for unique_keys growth rate > X% in 5m, 2) add paging backlog threshold autoscale, 3) improve on-call runbooks for paging drains.

jose: customer comms updated: "We rolled back a change and enabled mitigations; services restored. We will follow up with root-cause and timeline for permanent fix." Sending now.

sam_oncall: post-incident checklist:
- Incident owner: sam_oncall (initial triage)
- Mitigation: flag flip + rollback + node drains at 02:55-03:18 UTC
- Customer impact: ~2% streaming requests affected; two enterprise customers reported degraded streams; no data loss
- Root cause: batch_splitter produced combinatorial prefixes after PR#3456; missing normalization and lack of prefixes cap
- Next steps: permanent patch + tests (owner: alex), infra alerts & runbook updates (owner: li), postmortem write-up (owner: priya), customer follow-up (owner: jose)

sam_oncall: handing off to eng-oncall (post-mitigation). Closing active page. If anything regresses, reopen this thread or page on-call.

priya: I'll schedule a 1hr postmortem meeting for tomorrow and attach telemetry + logs.

marta: adding timeline snippet for PMF:
- 02:40 UTC - first metric anomaly
- 02:47 UTC - incident-bot created thread
- 02:55 UTC - flipped feature.batch_splitter.enabled=false
- 03:05 UTC - canary rollback started (5%)
- 03:12 UTC - canary stable, proceeding to full rollback
- 03:18 UTC - full rollback completed
- 03:40 UTC - metrics returned near baseline

sam_oncall: thanks team. will file a short summary in the incident tracker and attach to this thread. Good job on fast toggle and rollback coordination.

alex: +1, will follow up with patch PR and tests.

marta: closing monitoring loop.

(END OF THREAD)
